ABSTRACT: Herein, a rhodium-catalyzed highly chemo-, regio-, and
stereo-selective linear cross coupling reaction of terminal alkynes with
readily available 2,3-allenols aforded the synthetically and biologically
versatile 3-alkyn-2(E)-enones/enals. The reaction exhibits a perfect
match of the reactivities for these two classes of compounds since the
well-known self-reacting products of both reactants were not formed.
The reaction enjoys a wide substrate scope under ambient conditions.
Furthermore, the synthetic potentials have been demonstrated by
utilizing this reaction as a pivotal step: a very concise two-step total
synthesis of naturally occurring isotaxifolial D has been achieved; an
eficient synthesis of dehydroacitretin by applying this reaction two times
has also been executed. Through mechanistic studies including D-
labeling experiments, it is proposed that the reaction proceeded via

■ CONCLUSIONS
In summary, we have developed a conceptually new approach
for the enyne synthesis via a single rhodium-catalyzed cross-
coupling reaction of terminal alkynes with 2,3-allenols. This
protocol enables an eficient and highly selective preparation of
(E)-3-alkynyl enones/enals under a set of ambient conditions,
which could serve as platform molecules for the synthesis of
many other useful molecules due to the accommodation of a
wide array of highly reactive functional groups. The synthetic
potential of this methodology has been demonstrated via
derivatization of bio-active molecules, the eficient total
syntheses of isotaxifolial D, and the synthesis of dehydroaci
tretin. A mechanism has been proposed for the observed highly
selective formation of (E)-3-alkynyl enones/enals. The use of a
base is not required since the terminal alkynylmetalation
proceeds readily under base-free conditions, and the catalyti-
cally active rhodium catalyst has been regenerated via aerobic
oxidation with the help of HOAc. The development of many
other types of such reactions with both types of readily
available terminal alkynes and allenes as the reactants for enyne
syntheses is highly expected and is being actively pursued in
our laboratory.

(E)-3-alkynyl enones/enals under a set of ambient conditions,
which could serve as platform molecules for the synthesis of
many other useful molecules due to the accommodation of a
wide array of highly reactive functional groups. The synthetic
potential of this methodology has been demonstrated via
derivatization of bio-active molecules, the eficient total
syntheses of isotaxifolial D, and the synthesis of dehydroaci
tretin. A mechanism has been proposed for the observed highly
selective formation of (E)-3-alkynyl enones/enals. The use of a
base is not required since the terminal alkynylmetalation
proceeds readily under base-free conditions, and the catalyti-
cally active rhodium catalyst has been regenerated via aerobic
oxidation with the help of HOAc. The development of many
other types of such reactions with both types of readily
available terminal alkynes and allenes as the reactants for enyne
syntheses is highly expected and is being actively pursued in
our laboratory.
